page: Microsoft Azure D2als_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dalsv7 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, mapping to 1 physical core with 2 threads. The system is configured with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is in the top tier (top 10%) at 3584.27, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier results. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks but weak for small cached blocks. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are also positioned in the bottom 25%.

This server offers a low-memory, entry-level hardware profile, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require strong single-threaded CPU performance but have minimal memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the constrained 4.0 GB RAM and weak multi-core scaling. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic utility scripting, or small-scale web serving where high memory capacity and multi-threaded parallelization are not required.
